findings.issue: The asyncHandler wrapping rule is stated as a blanket architecture rule, but it is Express-specific (Fastify awaits handlers natively and forwards rejections to error handling; NestJS uses exception filters/interceptors instead). This sits uneasily against 'Editing discipline', which explicitly treats Express/Fastify/NestJS as interchangeable options already present in a given repo.
findings.recommendation: Scope the asyncHandler rule to Express, e.g. 'If the repo uses Express, wrap async route handlers in asyncHandler...; Fastify and NestJS handle this natively.'
